Here is a phenomenon which I find quite surprising. I believe it's the issue which underlies a lot of recent headaches in FLT so I hope to understand it properly. I have not yet minimised to be mathlib-free but I'm working on it.

Before I post it, I'll describe it. First you define abbrev myAdicCompletion := <a thing>, and then you try example : myAdicCompletion = <the same thing> := rfl. The proof takes far longer to elaborate than I would like, because Lean unfolds everything and the underlying terms are huge. Here's the code, plus the trace indicating that the unfolding is taking place.

abbrev causing unfolding (with mathlib)

import Mathlib

namespace IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum

variable {A : Type} (K : Type) [instField : Field K] [instCommRing : CommRing A]
    [instDedekindDomain : IsDedekindDomain A] [instAlgebra : Algebra A K]
    [instIsFractionRing : IsFractionRing A K]
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum A)

abbrev myAdicCompletion := (v.valuation K).Completion
--set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true in
--set_option trace.profiler true in
example : myAdicCompletion K v = (v.valuation K).Completion := rfl
/-
[Elab.command] [652240.000000] ✅️ example : myAdicCompletion K v = (v.valuation K).Completion :=
      rfl ▼
  ...

                  (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= UniformSpace.Completion (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼

                      (valuation K v)).toUniformSpace =?= (WithVal.instValued (valuation K v)).toUniformSpace ▼
                [] [192580.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instValued (valuation K v)).1 =?= (WithVal.instValued (valuation K v)).1 ▼
                  ...
                  [] [190573.000000] ✅️ IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace
                        (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼
                    [delta] [190447.000000] ✅️ IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace
                          (WithVal
                            (valuation K v)) =?= IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼

                                    (WithVal.valuation

Before I explain the reason why this is happening, let me show an abbrev-free instance of the phenomenon (still with mathlib). Here i1 and i2 are two terms of the Prop-valued mathlib class IsOrderedMonoid X (i.e. two proofs of the same theorem). We use these proofs to make two terms of the type-valued class LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero Y and then when we embed these classes in a more complex term, unfolding starts again.

two proofs of same theorem => unfolding

import Mathlib

namespace IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum

variable {A : Type} (K : Type) [instField : Field K] [instCommRing : CommRing A]
    [instDedekindDomain : IsDedekindDomain A] [instAlgebra : Algebra A K]
    [instIsFractionRing : IsFractionRing A K]
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum A)

theorem i1 : IsOrderedMonoid (Multiplicative ℤ) := inferInstance

theorem i2 : IsOrderedMonoid (Multiplicative ℤ) := inferInstance

--set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true in
--set_option trace.profiler true in
example :
    @Valuation.Completion (WithZero (Multiplicative Int))
      (@WithZero.instLinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (Multiplicative Int) _ _ i1) -- i1
      K _ (v.valuation K) =
    @Valuation.Completion (WithZero (Multiplicative Int))
      (@WithZero.instLinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (Multiplicative Int) _ _ i2) -- change proof
      K _ (v.valuation K) :=
  rfl
/-
    [Meta.isDefEq] [189326.000000] ✅️ (valuation K v).Completion =
          (valuation K v).Completion =?= (valuation K v).Completion = (valuation K v).Completion ▼
      [] [189038.000000] ✅️ (valuation K v).Completion =?= (valuation K v).Completion ▼
        [] [188826.000000] ✅️ UniformSpace.Completion
              (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= UniformSpace.Completion (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼
          [delta] [188706.000000] ✅️ UniformSpace.Completion
                (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= UniformSpace.Completion (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼
            (etc etc)
-/

I believe that the second code block unfolding is the reason that the first code block unfolds. For abbrev myAdicCompletion := (v.valuation K).Completion is something to do with valuations, and valuations are functions which take values in LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZeros; the group with zero in question is WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ), which needs a proof of IsOrderedMonoid (Multiplicative ℤ) (a Prop-valued class). But if you look at the LHS and RHS of the abbrev codeblock above with pp.all true, in the RHS the proof is found by typeclass inference, and in the LHS (the abbrev side) the proof is myAdicCompletion._proof_1, a second proof which the abbrev has magically concocted and which is of course defeq to the typeclass proof but, as the second code block shows, this is not enough to stop unfolding occurring.

I will work on a minimisation but I have limited time for working this week as I'm on holiday and I thought that maybe this was already enough for people to suggest possible workarounds.
But why do you want yourAdicCompletion to be an abbrev?
docs#IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion is an abbrev in mathlib and that's the actual problem. Working with it is painfully slow for this reason (sorry for not making that clearer!)

I haven't taken a close look at the traces yet but I assume all the other unfoldings are of projections? Both the elaborator and the kernel assume that abbrev and projections are cheaper to unfold than to attempt comparison arg-by-arg, yes

here https://gist.github.com/kbuzzard/934dadbb636fdc5d57325c038d1037d4 is an LLM's attempt to minimise. Everything is taking things in the algebra hierarchy apart, if that's what projections are. Some might not be fields of structures though.

Is this what you mean?

class foo (α : Type) : Prop where

instance bar : foo Nat := ⟨⟩

structure baz (α : Type) where
  pf   : foo α
  data : α → α

abbrev bazz : baz Nat := ⟨inferInstance, id⟩

#print bazz --@[reducible] def bazz : baz Nat := { pf := bazz._proof_1, data := id }

Even if the inferInstance is just bar, it is stored as bazz._proof_1, so when you prove that bazz = ⟨bar, id⟩ Lean has to unfold everything.

Yes exactly, the problem is that the abbrev abstracts away the proof that IsOrderedMonoid (Multiplicative ℤ) into myAdicCompletion._proof_1. And unfortunately, the unification algorithm doesn't have proof-irrelevance built in to the point of being able to instantly unify two expressions that only differ at some proofs.

An ad-hoc solution to the problem is to add the following shortcut instance:

instance : LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
  inferInstance

This doesn't stop unfolding for me. Am I doing it wrong?

import Mathlib

-- here?
instance : LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
  inferInstance

#check IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion

namespace IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum

variable (A K : Type*) [instField : Field K] [instCommRing : CommRing A]
    [instDedekindDomain : IsDedekindDomain A] [instAlgebra : Algebra A K]
    [instIsFractionRing : IsFractionRing A K]
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum A)

--set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true in
--set_option trace.profiler true in
example : adicCompletion K v = (v.valuation K).Completion := rfl
/-
      [] [194141.000000] ✅️ adicCompletion K v =?= (valuation K v).Completion ▼
        [] [193960.000000] ✅️ (valuation K v).Completion =?= (valuation K v).Completion ▼
          [] [193748.000000] ✅️ UniformSpace.Completion
                (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= UniformSpace.Completion (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼
            [delta] [193628.000000] ✅️ UniformSpace.Completion
                  (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= UniformSpace.Completion (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▼
              [] [975.000000] ✅️ WithVal (valuation K v) =?= WithVal (valuation K v) ▶
              [] [192511.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instValued
                      (valuation K v)).toUniformSpace =?= (WithVal.instValued (valuation K v)).toUniformSpace ▼
                [] [192333.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instValued (valuation K v)).1 =?= (WithVal.instValued (valuation K v)).1 ▼
                  [whnf] [14.000000] ✅️ Non-easy whnf: Valued (WithVal (valuation K v)) (WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ))
                  [whnf] [682.000000] ✅️ Non-easy whnf: WithVal.instValued (valuation K v) ▶
                  [whnf] [682.000000] ✅️ Non-easy whnf: WithVal.instValued (valuation K v) ▶
                  [] [190326.000000] ✅️ IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace
                        (WithVal (valuation K v)) =?= IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace (WithVal (valuation K v)) ▶
-/

(later addition): I tried it just after the declaration in mathlib and this didn't help either.

Aah -- if I put it just before the declaration in mathlib, and if I do not put 

instance : LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
  inferInstance

anywhere after this, then I get away with it -- unfolding no longer occurs.

With this change, we now have that writing

instance : LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
  inferInstance

just before

example : adicCompletion K v = (v.valuation K).Completion := rfl

makes it take 5 times as long to compile. Note that this is a Prop-valued class!(no it's not)
Yes exactly, I made #40750 to see if there are performance effects in mathlib.
What do you mean with it being a Prop-valued class? LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero is definitely type valued.

I think an underlying problem here is the fact that the class LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero even exists in the first place. We don't have the analogous LinearOrderedCommGroup. Don't you think that definitions like WithVal should just take the assumptions LinearOrder and CommGroup separately? And any theorems that require IsOrderedMonoid can add this assumption.

What do you mean with it being a Prop-valued class?

Oh, my error! I now understand why it works :-)

OK so I have confirmed that this change has a huge positive performance impact on FLT e.g. IsDedekindDomain.FiniteAdeleRing.baseChange_bijective goes down from 477094458 to 106459551 mHeartbeats. This might even close https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/issues/889 .

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

I think an underlying problem here is the fact that the class LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero even exists in the first place. We don't have the analogous LinearOrderedCommGroup. Don't you think that definitions like WithVal should just take the assumptions LinearOrder and CommGroup separately? And any theorems that require IsOrderedMonoid can add this assumption.

The challenge in unbundling it is that IsOrderedMonoid is too weak, you need to assert that Zero is Bot and mul and order compatible. Maybe now that we have a Zero is bot class, perhaps it is possible.
Aha, so we could add a Prop class that is the combination of PosMulStrictMono α, OrderBot α, IsBotZeroClass α
Removing LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero has been on my radar for a while. I believe it is easily doable now
Oh wait, OrderBot contains the data of a bot element. How would we set up the bot data in this?
The resulting speedup in #40750 is not very large, only improving a few files, but I could imagine that this will be much more impactful in FLT.
Correct, there is no class that asserts there is a bot without setting it.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

The resulting speedup in #40750 is not very large, only improving a few files, but I could imagine that this will be much more impactful in FLT.

Yes, I can remove a bunch of set_option maxHeartbeats 400000 in in FLT material which I want to PR to mathlib but have been holding off because proof elaboration was taking too long. I think that the the few files which it improves are all downstream of Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/AdicValuation.lean (and there are not that many files downstream from there). Note also that the largest change (30% speedup) is in the FiniteAdeleRing file and in FLT we have a huge amount of finite adele ring API which we've been developing for months, and which will be needed for class field theory and Tate's thesis as well as FLT.
